Pairwise genetic distances from PCA scores

Source: R/convenience_funcs.R
pca_dist.Rd

Runs a PCA on allele-frequency data from an adegenet::genind object and returns Euclidean distances computed on the retained principal component scores.

Usage

pca_dist(gi, n_axes = 64, scale = TRUE)

Arguments

gi

A genind object from adegenet.

n_axes

Number of principal component axes to retain. Capped at the total number of available axes.

scale

Logical. If TRUE (default), the resulting distance matrix is rescaled to [0, 1] via scale_to_0_1.

Value

A symmetric numeric distance matrix with one row/column per individual in gi.

Details

Missing genotypes in gi are imputed by the allele-mean method (equivalent to adegenet::tab(gi, NA.method = "mean")), then a standard PCA via prcomp is applied to the allele frequency table. Euclidean distances are then computed on the first n_axes scores.

This is a convenience wrapper designed for users who prefer to work from a genind object. For biallelic SNP data the more direct dist_from_biallelic is generally faster and does not require the adegenet package.

See also

dist_from_biallelic, cov_from_genetic_data

Other genetic responses: check_distance_response(), lower()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("adegenet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(nancycats, package = "adegenet")
  d <- pca_dist(nancycats, n_axes = 4)
  dim(d)
}
